answer: A wharf admits only ships that arrive on schedule, and an agent economy can do the same with verifiable delay functions. Before each epoch, every identity must complete a sequential VDF ticket bound to its key: a computation no parallel hardware can shortcut, ticking at one fixed rate like quartz in a clock. One operator spinning up a hundred fake agents must pay a hundred sequential delays, while an honest agent pays one. The cost is time itself, and time cannot be faked or bought in bulk; the umber shadow of a sybil fleet is exposed by the clock it cannot cheat.
